solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Head of government admits they used to support suspensions

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of government is used

parts.note: to admit someone in is to allow them

explanation.surface: A government chief concedes something about past support for suspended officials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspensions' reads as disciplinary suspensions, but it means hangings; the definition is past-tense because these structures are no longer used.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging frames were the structures from which condemned people were suspended at executions.

clue.text: White magic ingredient for a couple of lovers?

indicators.note: ingredient for says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A spell of good sorcery that might bring two lovers together.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossip columns call a romantically linked pair a single unit, as in 'they are now an item'.

clue.text: Pence on about seizing unpleasant person's capital

indicators.note: seizing means the rearranged letters grip the other piece inside them
about signals that the letters of Pence on are moved around into a new order

parts.note: a hag is an ugly, unpleasant old woman

explanation.surface: Mike Pence fusses about grabbing a nasty person's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the letters of 'Pence on' into COPENEN. 'Capital' looks like money but is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Copenhagen is the chief city and seat of government of Denmark.

clue.text: Amis's novel about heroin and power: Blow

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters wrap around the next piece
novel means new or fresh, so the letters of Amis appear in a fresh order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
H is drug slang for heroin
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A Martin Amis novel about drugs and power, with blow as cocaine slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges AMIS into MISA; 'about' puts H inside it, giving MISHA, then P follows. 'Blow' looks like cocaine slang but means a setback.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow is a misfortune or setback, an unlucky accident.

clue.text: Our mag, crafty thing that emphasizes optics

parts.note: the clue appears in Private Eye, so the setter's own magazine is the Eye
playfully, something craft-like: an ocean liner is a sea craft

explanation.surface: Our magazine's cunning trick that draws attention to how things look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crafty' looks like cunning but is read as 'of the craft sort', a liner being a ship. 'Optics' are here the eyes themselves, not public image.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic pencil drawn along the lash line makes the eyes stand out.

clue.text: Murders on the rise, mark

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to top someone is slang for killing them

explanation.surface: A rising murder rate leaves its mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rise' turns TOPS into SPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a small stain or mark on a surface.

clue.text: Cocaine and grass under desk — official!

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under something means coming after it

parts.note: a bureau is a writing desk
C is drug slang for cocaine
a grass and a rat are both slang for an informer

explanation.surface: Drugs hidden under an office desk shock a pen-pusher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like cannabis beside cocaine, but it is an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureaucrat is an administrative functionary in government service.

clue.text: Echo's newsworthy material — "Pussy!"

parts.note: journalists call material fit to print copy
pussy is a familiar word for a cat

explanation.surface: A tabloid called the Echo shouting abuse in a headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Echo' looks like a newspaper's name, but it is the definition: someone who echoes others.
explanation.definitionFit: An imitator repeats what others do, as an echo repeats a sound.

clue.text: Connoisseur writer on sex: "Yes!"

parts.note: an author is a writer
it is old slang for sex appeal or sex

explanation.surface: An expert author of erotica gives an enthusiastic yes.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert or acknowledged specialist on a subject is called an authority.

clue.text: Mickey's pet small place — moving out

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, a shortened form

indicators.note: moving means the letters of out shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Mickey's pet rents a small home and is about to move out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges OUT into UTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney's cartoon dog belongs to Mickey Mouse.

clue.text: Bounder at the wrong South London district

parts.note: a young sheep is something that bounds or skips about

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of the word the are put out of order

explanation.surface: A cad behaving badly in a South London borough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' looks like an old word for a cad, but it means something that leaps, a lamb. 'wrong' turns THE into ETH.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambeth is a borough on the south bank of the Thames.

clue.text: Swimmer suffocated by heartless sex partner becomes a national draw?

indicators.note: being suffocated by something means being wrapped up inside it
heartless means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: a lay is slang for a sexual partner
an otter is an aquatic swimming mammal

explanation.surface: A swimmer smothered by a cold-hearted lover becomes a national attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sex partner' looks like part of the surface story; a 'lay' is slang. The UK's National Lottery is a prize draw.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize draw run nationally by ticket sale, such as Britain's National Lottery.

clue.text: (&28dn.) Chain put on hound after joker Farage claims to be victim of one

definitions.text: Farage claims to be victim of one

indicators.note: after says the joker comes before the rest
put on says the chain piece goes in front of the hound piece

parts.note: a wit is a joker or wag
CH is the abbreviation for chain, an old unit of length
to hound someone is to hunt them down

explanation.surface: A chain on a dog, with Farage claiming persecution.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigel Farage is a British politician who often says he is being persecuted. 'Chain' looks like a dog lead but is the abbreviation CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign of persecution against a supposed wrongdoer, named after witch-finder trials.

clue.text: One who's quick to cherish prat — it makes you weep!

indicators.note: to cherish is to hold close, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: a tearer is one who tears along, moving fast
a prat and a jerk are both an idiot

explanation.surface: A fast mover devoted to a fool, which is enough to make you cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cherish' reads as affection, but it signals holding one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentimental film or story designed to make its audience cry.

clue.text: Dick welcomes new Ukrainian "less awkward" leaders — it sticks out a mile, maybe

definitions.text: it sticks out a mile, maybe

indicators.note: welcomes means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: dick is slang for the male member

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A man welcomes a Ukrainian who is less clumsy, with a rude double meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition's innuendo hides land jutting into the sea; the question mark admits it is only a 'maybe' mile.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland projecting far into the sea is a strip of land nearly surrounded by water.

clue.text: Tory row not resolved? Never mind

indicators.note: resolved means the letters are broken down and settled into a new order

explanation.surface: A Conservative quarrel left unsettled, but it hardly matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are phrases telling someone a matter is no cause for concern.

clue.text: Fit to go round King's Row

indicators.note: to go round means the first piece encircles the second

parts.note: an ague is a fever fit with shivering
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Something fit to surround the King's road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a street, but it means a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A row is a quarrel, a heated dispute.

clue.text: Don't expect Trump to produce this show about sources of dire economy

definitions.text: Don't expect Trump to produce this

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the next

parts.note: to evince is to show or display

indicators.note: sources are origins, so the opening letters of each word

explanation.surface: Trump is unlikely to back his claims about a dire economy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a satirical jibe: Trump is said never to produce proof for his claims.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof or supporting facts, which the satirical clue says Trump never offers.

clue.text: Turner, right after Tory leader punches Joey

indicators.note: after says the right piece follows the rest
punches means one piece is driven into the middle of another

parts.note: a joey is a baby kangaroo, a roo

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Tory leader punching someone called Joey, with a painter named Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like the painter but is something that turns. 'punches' puts T inside ROO.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine, something that spins.

clue.text: One-time lover, rather large, giving a specimen

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
ample means generously large

explanation.surface: A portly former lover provides a sample.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance representative of its kind, a typical sample.

clue.text: Rock's more brassy sound

indicators.note: sound means the word is heard rather than read, a word with the same pronunciation

parts.note: brassy means bold and brazen, so more brassy is bolder

explanation.surface: Rock music gets a louder, more brassy sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like music, but it is a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A large rounded stone, a big chunk of rock.

clue.text: President's 'Team Jack' elected to send a message alert

parts.note: XI is the Roman numeral eleven, a cricket or football team
J is the card abbreviation for jack
a candidate elected is in
to ping is to send an alert notification

explanation.surface: A president's team elected to notify everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The leader of China holds the title of state president.

clue.text: Wine holder (spit allowed)

parts.note: gob is slang for spit
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A wine glass where spitting is permitted, as at a tasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A stemmed drinking cup for wine.

clue.text: In the open air, having no alternative, come first

indicators.note: having no means a piece is removed

parts.note: outdoor means in the open air
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Outside, with no other choice, someone wins.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass or beat rivals is to win, finishing ahead.

clue.text: Wonder if account left in bog

indicators.note: in means the following pieces sit inside the bog piece

parts.note: a mire is a bog

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a bill was left in the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bog' looks like British slang for a toilet, but it is a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A marvel or supernatural event that causes amazement.

clue.text: Politicians? Cheats

definitions.meaning: Short for Conservatives, members of a UK party
a con is a swindle, so to con is to cheat

explanation.definitionFit: Short for Conservative Party members, and also a verb for tricking people.

clue.text: Disreputable place that's changed monk's political allegiance?

indicators.note: changed means one letter is swapped for another
political allegiance means right is swapped for left

parts.note: a brother is a monk, a member of a religious order

explanation.surface: A monk defects politically and ends up somewhere shady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed political allegiance' swaps R (right) for L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: A house of ill repute, where sex is sold.

clue.text: see 13ac.
Rest gets elected after 'fake news!'

indicators.note: after says elected follows the fake news piece

parts.note: a lie is fake news, an untruth
a candidate elected is in

explanation.surface: A politician who complains of fake news yet still wins a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying late in bed in the morning.

clue.text: Plain Trump colleague not against the evicting of people?

parts.note: plain means clear

indicators.note: not means a letter is removed

parts.note: JD Vance is Trump's vice-president
V is short for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: A Trump colleague being plainly not against evicting people.
explanation.walkthrough: The Highland Clearances were the mass eviction of Scottish tenants.
explanation.definitionFit: Removal of tenants from land, as in the Scottish Highland Clearances.
